Seven deuterium discharges from the JET tokamak with the ITER-like wall were studied, with line-averaged densities spanning 2-5.5 x 10^19 m^-3.
The L-H transition power threshold P_L-H varied by a factor of 2 between 3.4 MW and 6.6 MW across the discharges.
Larger upper triangularity δ_u resulted in a higher P_L-H, consistent with previous observations.
At ρ = 0.85 and 0.9, trapped electron modes (TEMs) propagating in both the electron and ion drift direction were observed at the lowest densities.
At higher densities, ion temperature gradient (ITG) modes were dominant, some of which exhibited trapped-ion drive and unconventional ballooning structures.
The experimental collisionality range corresponded to a region of minimum linear drive between ITG-TEM and resistive mode branches.
The quasilinear particle flux was directed inward only in the collisionality domain where the linear drive was minimized at ρ = 0.85 for all densities and 0.9 only for the highest densities.
QuaLiKiz was found to be inadequate beyond ρ = 0.85, while TGLF-SAT2 agreed well with the linear spectra and quasilinear heat fluxes from GENE up to and including ρ = 0.9.
